questions: Do oval completions hold at 14 of 20 or better with the wider ±0.07 m span?
Does slalom line_loss_events fall below 0.25 (iteration 7 at ±0.06 m gave 0.30)?
Does either the s-bend or the slalom produce any completion, or any run above progress 0.5?
If oval completions fall while line loss falls, is the span too wide for the weights, so the signal needs rescaling rather than a geometry change?

intent: Restore the 16 mm footprint that gave 14 of 20 oval completions, and widen the seven-sensor span from ±0.06 m to ±0.07 m (pitch about 0.0233 m) to add margin before the outer edge on the s-bend and slalom. The body, mass, track, wheel radius and row height stay at the iteration 7 values.
learning: Iteration 8 showed that a 12 mm footprint removes oval completions entirely (0 of 20 at 12 mm vs 14 of 20 at 16 mm), so the 16 mm footprint is necessary for the oval. Slalom line loss at 12 mm was 0.25, only slightly lower than the 0.30 at 16 mm, so the footprint is not the main slalom cause. The next lever is the outer span: if a wider span lowers slalom line loss without losing oval completions, the sharp-bend losses come from edge margin. If it does not, the limit is turn authority, which the Integrator should address with wheel_track or gains.
rationale: Iteration 8 settled the footprint question. Going from 16 mm to 12 mm at the same positions dropped oval completions from 14 of 20 to 0 of 20 (score 303.8 to 101.4), and slalom line loss only fell from 0.30 to 0.25. The Integrator's rule says to return to 16 mm when oval completions fall below about 12 of 20, so I revert sensor_size to 0.016 m. The 16 mm footprint is the only sensing setting that has produced completions. The s-bend and slalom still end off track at progress 0.27 and 0.12. Their failures look like sharp-bend losses at the outer edge, and the Integrator reports slalom line loss still at 0.25 or more. The next test is therefore the outer span. I widen the seven sensors to x = ±0.07 m, spread evenly at a pitch of about 0.0233 m, which is a small change from the 0.02 m pitch. I keep the iteration 7 mass, body, track, wheel radius and row height (y = 0.02 m) so that the only geometry change is the span. Expected result: oval completions hold near 14 of 20, slalom line_loss_events fall below 0.25, and the wider margin gives the s-bend and slalom their first chance of progress above 0.3. Max_error on the oval finishes is 0.048, so the oval is not expected to fall. The Integrator will need to rescale sensor weights to the wider span, since the signal is set by the weights.
